statement: Spaced retrieval practice improves delayed recall relative to rereading when total study time is matched, and the effect varies with retention interval.

scope.population: adult learners enrolled in introductory university courses
scope.measurement_time: 14 days after the final study session
scope.comparator: rereading with matched total study time

predictions: The advantage over rereading is larger on delayed than immediate tests under matched exposure.
falsifiers: A preregistered independent comparison finds no practically relevant delayed-recall advantage under matched study time and equivalent feedback.
alternative_hypotheses: Differences in feedback, expectancy, or test familiarity explain the observed advantage.
null_model: Matched study time and baseline ability fully explain delayed recall, with no additional effect of retrieval practice.
decision_context: Prioritize a falsifiable research question for a six-month project.
